facts.fact: Cibercidadãos, MISA Moçambique and AMIRGE refer to the existing Lei do Direito à Informação as already guaranteeing liberties that vague terms in the new cyber laws could restrict.

MOZ.note: The letter says the cyber bills do not cover AI-based crimes or deepfakes; no AI rule or authority is stated.
Nothing on AI use in government administration.
Nothing on AI in a sector's public system.
Nothing on AI built or hosted in Mozambique.

systems.system: Equipa Nacional de Resposta a Incidentes de Segurança Cibernética

MOZ.note: The national council, authority and response team are only proposed in a bill; no strategy adopted or body created is stated.

facts.fact: The letter says the Cybersecurity bill and the Cybercrime bill are under parliamentary appraisal by the Assembleia da República.
facts.system: Proposta de Lei de Segurança Cibernética and Proposta de Lei de Crimes Cibernéticos

facts.fact: Cibercidadãos, MISA Moçambique and AMIRGE publicly criticised the government's Cybercrime bill in a letter to the Assembly President, objecting to article 18 seizures without warrant and article 19 interception.
facts.system: Proposta de Lei de Crimes Cibernéticos
